brief-1.text: Identifies the true cause: the auto-crash on FV3/FV4 driven by the new inline density meters (fitted July 28) is starting the cold crash too early (9-10 days vs 13-15 on hydrometer-crashed tanks), cutting fermentation short before the yeast reabsorbs diacetyl. Must cite the tank split (5 of 6 FV3/FV4 batches buttery, 0 of 6 FV1/FV2) together with the shortened days-to-crash, and use batch 9 (FV3, controller in manual, 15 days, clean) as the internal control. A strong reply recommends checking the meters against hydrometer readings and/or a forced diacetyl test before crashing, not buying new yeast.

Rejects the yeast lot (L22) as the cause, with evidence: batch 2 was on the old lot L19 and still came out buttery, and six L22 batches (3, 5, 6, 9, 10, 12) are clean, all in FV1/FV2 or with a manual crash. Spending $1,800 to switch labs would not fix it. A reply that endorses dumping L22 misses this key.

Rejects the new brewer (Pia) as the cause, with evidence: her batches in FV1/FV2 (6, 10) are clean, while Marta's and Arlo's batches in FV3/FV4 (7, 11) are buttery. Her 3-of-5 share is explained by tank assignment, not her practice. A reply that leaves suspicion on Pia, or recommends retraining her, misses this key.

brief-2.text: Identifies the true cause: one or more of the four isolation valves from the September 4 Ardent Avenue repair was left partly or fully closed (or reopened incorrectly), changing flow direction and velocity into Linden Heights and scouring iron deposits from its unlined cast-iron mains. Must tie together the timing (complaints from September 5, the day after), the concentration (54 of 63 in Linden Heights), the zone-specific pressure drop (49-53 psi vs 60-64 in June, Hollis Park unchanged), and the iron-dominant samples. A strong reply recommends physically verifying the four valve positions (turn counts) and a hydrant flow test before the council meeting.

Rejects Well 7 as the cause, with evidence: it blends into the whole system but complaints cluster in one zone; plant effluent manganese is unchanged; the discoloration is iron (0.6-1.1 mg/L) while Well 7's iron is only 0.04 mg/L, and sample manganese (0.02-0.03) is below the level that typically discolors water. Taking Well 7 offline would not fix it. A reply that endorses the shutdown misses this key.

Rejects the Hollis Park flushing as the cause of the main problem, with evidence: complaints began September 5, four days before flushing started on September 9; flushing was in Hollis Park while 54 of 63 complaints are in Linden Heights; Hollis Park pressure is unchanged. At most, flushing or the lead service line work explains Hollis Park's 6 complaints. A reply that blames the flushing for Linden Heights misses this key.

brief-3.text: Identifies the true cause: the Android 5.2 release (August 31) with the billing library upgrade broke purchase handling, so trial conversions on Android are being reversed or refunded automatically (for example, purchases not acknowledged and then auto-refunded by the store, or entitlements not granted). Must cite the Play Console refunds jumping about 15x while App Store refunds stayed flat, Android being about 60% of trials, and the timing. A strong reply recommends splitting conversion by platform and app version and checking purchase acknowledgement or entitlement logs as the confirming test, and treats the rise in billing tickets as a possible symptom of failed purchases rather than price anger.

Rejects the price rise as the main cause, with evidence: Brazil, India and Mexico had no price change yet fell as much or more (33% to 20%) than the regions that got the price rise (41% to 31%); App Store refunds are flat even though iOS users in the US/UK/EU saw the same price rise. Rolling back the price would not restore conversion. A reply that endorses the rollback as the fix misses this key.

Rejects the new onboarding flow as the cause, with evidence: conversion is essentially identical across the test arms (29.4% control vs 28.7% new flow), so the overall drop hit both arms equally; the lower day-3 practice rate has not shown up in conversion. Killing the test would not restore conversion. A reply that endorses killing the flow to fix the drop misses this key.
